श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता:
*
सिवाय अन्य किसी उपायका सहारा नहीं लिया। अन्य
उपायोंकी तरफ उसकी दृष्टि ही नहीं गयी । उसने केवल
भगवान्‌का ही सहारा लिया * । तात्पर्य यह हुआ कि
सकामभाव रहनेपर भी आर्त भक्त उसकी पूर्ति केवल
भगवान्से ही चाहते हैं ।
जो भगवान्‌के साथ अपनापन करके भगवान्‌के
परायण हैं और अनुकूलताकी वैसी इच्छा नहीं करते; पर
प्रतिकूल परिस्थिति आनेपर इच्छा हो जाती है कि
भगवान्ने ऐसा क्यों किया ? ' यह प्रतिकूलता मिट जाय तो
बहुत अच्छा है।' इस प्रकार प्रतिकूलता मिटानेका भाव पैदा
होनेसे वे भी आर्त भक्त कहलाते हैं ।
(३) जिज्ञासु भक्त - जिसमें अपने स्वरूपको,
भगवत्तत्त्वको जाननेकी जोरदार इच्छा जाग्रत् हो जाती है
कि वास्तवमें मेरा स्वरूप क्या है ? भगवत्तत्त्व क्या है ?
इस प्रकार तत्त्वको जाननेके लिये शास्त्र, गुरु अथवा
पुरुषार्थ (श्रवण, मनन, निदिध्यासन आदि उपायों) का भी
आश्रय न रखते हुए केवल भगवान्‌के आश्रित होकर उस
तत्त्वको केवल भगवान् से ही जो जानना चाहते हैं; वे
जिज्ञासु भक्त कहलाते हैं ।
जिज्ञासु भक्त वही होता है, जिसका जिज्ञास्य केवल
भगवत्तत्त्व और उपाय केवल भगवद्भक्ति ही होती है
अर्थात् उपेय और उपायमें अनन्यता होती है ।
जिज्ञासु भक्तोंमें उद्धवजीका नाम लिया जाता है।
भगवान्ने उद्धवजीको दिव्यज्ञानका उपदेश दिया था, जो
‘उद्धवगीता' (श्रीमद्भागवत ११ । ७–३०) के नामसे
प्रसिद्ध है।

दृष्टि थी, दूसरोंका भरोसा था, अपने बलका सहारा था, तबतक वह कष्ट पाती रही । परन्तु जब दूसरोंकी तरफसे तो क्या,

The implication is that even when one is sakama (attached to worldly desires), the artharthi (one who is seeking material wealth) bhaktas (devotees) want to fulfill their desires only from the Lord.

Those who have a sense of belonging with the Lord and are devoted to the Lord, and do not have such a desire for convenience, but when faced with adversity, they have a desire that the Lord did this, 'If this adversity could be removed, it would be good.' (3) The jijnyasu (inquisitive) bhaktas - In which a strong desire to know one's true nature and the nature of the Lord arises, 'What is my true nature? What is the nature of the Lord?' In this way, without taking the support of scriptures, gurus, or means of self-realization (such as shravana, manana, nididhyasana, etc.), they take only the support of the Lord and want to know this truth only from the Lord; they are called jijnyasu bhaktas.

The jijnyasu bhaktas are those who have only the Lord's nature as their object of inquiry and only the means of devotion to the Lord as their means. In other words, there is non-dualism in the means and the object.

The name of Udhhav is mentioned among the jijnyasu bhaktas. The Lord had given Udhhav divine knowledge, which is famous as 'Udhhav Gita' (Shrimad Bhagavat 11.7-30).

(4)
Jijnyasu - To explain the uniqueness of the jnani (wise) bhaktas (devotees) compared to the three types of bhaktas mentioned earlier, the word 'cha' (and) is used here.

Jnani (wise) bhaktas - The jnani bhaktas see all favorable and unfavorable circumstances, events, people, and objects as the Lord's own form. In other words, they see all circumstances as the Lord's play. Just as the Lord never has any desire to achieve anything for Himself, nor does He have any desire to remove any adversity, nor does He have any desire to attain knowledge, the jnani bhaktas also do not have any such desires. They are completely immersed in the Lord's love.

The name of the gopis (cowherd girls) is famous among the jnani bhaktas. The sage Narada has also mentioned them as an ideal of jnani bhaktas in the Bhakti Sutra (21), saying 'yatha vrajagopikanam' (just like the gopis of Vrindavan). The reason is that the gopis had completely renounced their own happiness. Their happiness was only in the Lord's happiness.

One thing to understand is that those who are attached to the Lord due to their desire for wealth, their desire to remove suffering, and their desire to fulfill their inquiry are considered bhaktas. However, those who have the idea that wealth can be obtained through other means, suffering can be removed through other means, and inquiry can be fulfilled through other means, do not have a sense of belonging with the Lord, and therefore, they do not have love for the Lord, and they are not considered bhaktas.

The saints say that love is only that which the Lord Himself has, and the devotee only has a sense of belonging with the Lord. The reason is that love is that which never takes anything from anyone. The Lord has given Himself to all beings, and He has no attachment to anyone. Those who have a sense of belonging with the Lord and are immersed in the Lord's love are considered jnani bhaktas. However, sometimes, due to association with others, or due to their own nature, they may have a desire to know their true nature and the nature of the Lord. They are also considered jijnyasu.

There was a vision, there was trust in others, there was reliance on one's own strength, until then she suffered. But when there was no reliance on others, and there was no reliance on one's own strength, then her ananya (non-dual) nature arose, and she did not suffer.

Similarly, Gajendra suffered for years as long as he relied on the strength of elephants and tigresses. When all support was lost, and only the support of the Lord remained, he did not suffer.

* Obeisance, obeisance to the great yogi, the Lord of the gods, the Lord of the universe. I do not see any other refuge except for you. Wherever there is death, it is due to mutual enmity. (Shrimad Bhagavat 1.8.9-10)
'O Lord, O Lord of the gods, O Lord of the universe, O great yogi! Protect me, protect me. I do not see any other refuge except for you in this world, because everyone is causing death to each other. O Lord, O Lord of the universe, this burning arrow is coming towards me. O Lord, even if it burns me, do not destroy my embryo.'
